To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
interactive and non-interactive media stimuli elicits different patterns of recovery experiences.
the enjoyment of entertaining interactive and noninteractive stimuli is associated with different patterns of recovery experiences and outcomes.
the use of interactive media is associated with greater need satisfaction and better recovery than the use of noninteractive media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the enjoyment of interactive media on recovery.
the recovery experience of individuals after they have been engaged in a demanding working task.
the effects of the enjoyment of media on human well-being and the satisfaction of intrinsic psychological needs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has provided evidence of a positive effect of interactive and non-interactive entertaining media use on recovery experience, enjoyment and recovery outcomes, but that the effects of interactive media use on recovery and recovery outcomes may not be stronger than non-interactive media use.
the present investigation provides evidence for the satisfaction of intrinsic psychological needs through the use entertainment media and that these effects are related to recovery outcomes.
the present study demonstrates that the use of entertaining and nonentertaining media may be associated with the recovery experience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of interactive media (i.e., video games) may be a more effective way to recover than noninteractive media (i.e. videos).
media use can be an important source of recovery and that the recovery effects are mediated by the satisfaction of recovery related needs.
the use of interactive media may be more effective in eliciting a recovery experience than the use of non-interactive media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of media is not only enjoyable, but also beneficial in terms of recovery and psychological well-being.
media enjoyment may be more than just a hedonic response.
the use of entertaining interactive media is a good way to recover from the negative effects of a working task.
